question: Is our support ticket data current enough to act on today?

input.purpose: Check freshness of Zendesk ticket data: latest sync, latest ticket create/update timestamps, and row counts.
input.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
       MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS max_fivetran_synced,
       MAX(created_at) AS max_created_at,
       MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at,
       SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_deleted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS deleted_rows
FROM zendesk.ticket

input.purpose: Look at daily ticket volume and sync activity over the last 3 weeks to see whether the feed has gaps.
input.sql:
SELECT CAST(_fivetran_synced AS DATE) AS sync_day,
       COUNT(*) AS rows_synced,
       MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at_in_batch
FROM zendesk.ticket
WHERE _fivetran_synced >= TIMESTAMP '2026-10-15'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

input.purpose: Check ticket created/updated volume by day in late October and early November, and compare sync timestamps across other source tables to see if the 2026-11-09 sync stamp is an anomaly.
input.sql:
SELECT CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_day, COUNT(*) AS tickets, MIN(_fivetran_synced) AS min_sync, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS max_sync
FROM zendesk.ticket
WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-10-25'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

input.purpose: Compare latest sync timestamps across other source tables to see whether the whole pipeline is stamped in the future or only Zendesk.
input.sql:
SELECT 'zendesk.ticket' AS src, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS max_sync FROM zendesk.ticket
UNION ALL SELECT 'zendesk.organization', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM zendesk.organization
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.account
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.opportunity', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.opportunity
UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.vbak', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM sap_s4.vbak
UNION ALL SELECT 'carrier_pg.shipment', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM carrier_pg.shipment

input.purpose: Measure typical daily ticket creation volume over the last 60 days to judge whether the zero tickets on Nov 4-6 are unusual.
input.sql:
SELECT CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_day, DAYNAME(CAST(created_at AS DATE)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS tickets
FROM zendesk.ticket
WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-09-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

answer.answer_summary: Not confirmed current. The newest support ticket activity in Zendesk is from Tuesday 3 Nov 2026 (last update 18:00 UTC), about three days before the 6 Nov as-of date, and no tickets appear for 4-6 Nov, which is unusual. The sync timestamps say data was loaded on 9-11 Nov, which is after today, so they cannot be used to confirm freshness. Check the Zendesk-to-warehouse feed before acting on ticket data today.

assumptions: As-of date is Friday 6 Nov 2026, as stated in the instructions.
Freshness is judged from business timestamps (created_at / updated_at) because the _fivetran_synced values are later than the as-of date.
The ticket table has no deletions (0 rows flagged _fivetran_deleted), so no records were removed from the view.
Zero tickets on 4-6 Nov is treated as a possible feed gap, not as a real drop in support demand, because it is out of pattern with the prior two months.
caveats: The sync timestamps are 3 to 5 days in the future across all six sources I checked, so the connector clock or timestamp handling is likely wrong. I cannot tell from the data when ticket data was really last loaded.
Three days with no tickets is unusual for this table but not impossible. It could be a real lull or a source-side issue. I could not confirm which.
Ticket volume is low (typically 1-15 per day), so single-day counts are noisy.
I did not check whether Zendesk itself has records after 3 Nov. That would need direct access to the Zendesk source.

explanation.title: Counted cancelled deliveries
explanation.detail: The SAP tables keep 310 cancelled deliveries as soft-deleted rows (_fivetran_deleted = true). This query never filters them out, so cancelled deliveries count as late.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.vbak', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM sap_s4.vbak

explanation.title: Missed a customer split across two CRM accounts
explanation.detail: Halbrook Fluid Systems has a look-alike duplicate account ("… GmbH") with no SAP number. Two of its open shipping tickets sit on the duplicate, so the customer looked healthy.

explanation.title: Read every history row of the account tier
explanation.detail: salesforce.account keeps one row per version of each account (history mode). Without filtering to _fivetran_active, accounts that changed tier appear twice, and Quenmere Paper Mills GmbH still looks Strategic.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced) FROM salesforce.account
